cohort: The study included 552 mothers with children aged 0 to 5 years in Rio Branco, Acre, Brazil, interviewed between 2007 and 2008.
finding: The study revealed a high rate of teenage pregnancy and found that arterial hypertension was the leading postpartum complication among women who had undergone a caesarean section.
mod_finding: Mothers who underwent caesarean section had a higher prevalence of hypertension (71.1%) during the postpartum period, with an adjusted prevalence ratio of 3.90 (95% CI [2.00, 7.61]) compared to others.
